# Context

Wheat trial WH09 (Wongan Hills, Western Australia, 2009): a resolvable row-column design with 2 replicates (columns 1 to 6 and 7 to 12) of 34 rows each. **Question:** does modelling rows and columns remove field variation?

```{r packages}
library(dplyr)
library(lme4)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r data}
wheat <- readr::read_csv("data/wheat_Australia_2008_2009_7loc.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
wh09 <- wheat %>% filter(Trial == "WH09") %>% mutate(across(c(rep, row, col, geno), factor))
glimpse(wh09)
```

```{r map}
ggplot(wh09, aes(as.integer(row), as.integer(col), fill = yield)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") + geom_hline(yintercept = 6.5, linewidth = 1) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() + labs(x = "Row", y = "Column", fill = "t/ha")
```

**Your findings:** where is the field variation: along rows or along columns? _...write here..._

# Two models

```{r fit}
m_rcbd <- lm(yield ~ rep + geno, data = wh09)

# HINT: row and column numbers repeat in each replicate, so write them within replicate: rep:row and rep:col
m_rowcol <- lmer(yield ~ rep + geno + (1 | rep:___) + (1 | rep:___), data = wh09)   # TODO

c(RCBD = sigma(m_rcbd)^2, row_column = sigma(m_rowcol)^2)
print(VarCorr(m_rowcol), comp = "Variance")
```

**Your findings:** how much smaller is the residual variance? Which is larger, the variance between rows or between columns? Does that agree with the map? _...write here..._
